# `Q-2-9` — HTML Element Auto-converted

> An HTML element written directly in markdown was passed through
> as raw HTML. Warning only.

## What this means

Writing HTML directly in markdown — "naked" HTML — is not a
supported form in Quarto Markdown. Quarto does not reject it: it
passes the element through unchanged and emits this warning so the
implicit conversion is visible.

How it is passed through depends on where the tag sits:

- A tag that **opens a line** and names a **block-level** element
  (`<div>`, `<details>`, `<summary>`, `<section>`, `<table>`, …)
  becomes a raw HTML *block*. It is emitted on its own, not wrapped
  in a paragraph — a `<div>` inside a `<p>` is invalid HTML, and a
  browser would silently restructure the page around it.
- Anything else — a tag in the middle of a sentence, or an inline
  element such as `<span>`, `<b>` or `<img>` — becomes a raw HTML
  *inline* and stays inside its paragraph.

## Why this happens

The pattern shows up whenever raw HTML appears in markdown text:

- A custom HTML element copied from elsewhere.
- A `<span>` or `<div>` used for styling.
- Embedded widget markup.

## How to fix

The warning does not block the build, so no action is strictly
required. To silence it, use one of the explicit forms.

For a block, either a raw-HTML block:

````markdown
```{=html}
<details class="checksums-section">
<summary>SHA-256 checksums</summary>
```
````

or — usually better, when all you want is a container with
attributes — a Quarto div, which is native markdown and works in
every output format:

```markdown
::: {.checksums-section}
Content here.
:::
```

For an inline, Pandoc's raw-attribute form:

```markdown
`<custom-tag>content</custom-tag>`{=html}
```
